metadata.method: Fresh process per case/build/round; first-use collections retained separately; two extra warmups per engine; alternating CPU/Metal timed order; process/build order rotated per round; inputs and exact CPU-reference validation untimed; complete result materialization timed; result release untimed.
metadata.scope: Development mechanisms only, not external-suite evidence or a general GPU speedup. Chain32 includes fusion advantages over the current CPU executor.
metadata.data: Row mechanisms use a deterministic 1024-value numeric distribution. Algorithm cases use Int32 keys: group_hash has min(N,1024) classes; group_high, join_hash and sort_radix have max(1,N/2) classes. Base keys are (37*i) modulo cardinality; sorted keys are monotone bins. Null variants invalidate every twentieth key; grouped values additionally invalidate every thirteenth row. Grouped sums use i modulo 17 minus 8; sort and self-left-join carry original Int64 row IDs. Float32 row values are exact multiples of 1/1024.
limitations: No external-suite coverage claimed; Float64 and floating reductions are outside these cases. Algorithm comparisons preserve complete output order and values against CPU.
First use includes context/shader initialization but is not a cold machine or cold filesystem measurement.
CPU and GPU share host memory and power limits; short timings can vary with scheduler and thermal state.
The Mojo profile is a separate warm collection after timed samples; complete caller-wall timing remains the performance measure.
Workload exposure: chain32 was used during fusion development; other cases broaden mechanism coverage without a holdout claim.
